source_refs.note: C) Phenyl Amine (Aromatic Amine): a main subheading of 24.2 Preparation of Amines, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 120-122.

items: Phenyl amine can be prepared by ammonolysis of chlorobenzene. Ammonolysis is a reaction in which an ammonia molecule is broken down to react with another compound.

blocks.alt: Chlorobenzene (benzene ring with Cl) + 2NH3, with Cu2O over and 250 degrees C, 50 atm under the arrow, gives phenylamine (ring with NH2) + NH4Cl.
blocks.caption: Ammonolysis of chlorobenzene to phenylamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 121).

items: Phenyl amine can also be prepared by the reduction of nitrobenzene.
book_errors: Phenyl amine can also be prepared by the reduction of nitrobenzene.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book numbers the methods of preparing phenyl amine i., iii. and iv.; there is no ii. They are three methods in a row: i., ii. and iii.

blocks.alt: Nitrobenzene (ring with NO2) + 6[H], with Sn + Conc. HCl over the arrow, gives phenyl amine (aniline) (ring with NH2) + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Reduction of nitrobenzene to phenyl amine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 122).

items: Phenyl amine can be prepared by the Hofmann reaction.
book_errors: Phenyl amine can be prepared by the Hofmann reaction.

blocks.alt: Hofmann reaction in one line: benzamide (ring with C(=O)-NH2) + Br2 + 4NaOH gives phenylamine (ring with NH2) + 2NaBr + Na2CO3 + 2H2O.
blocks.caption: Hofmann reaction of benzamide (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 122).

blocks.prompt: a) The “feel good factor” in chocolate has been identified as 2-phenylethanamine, C₆H₅CH₂CH₂NH₂. Suggest a synthesis of this compound from chloromethylbenzene, C₆H₅CH₂Cl.
blocks.explanation:
Heat C₆H₅CH₂Cl under reflux with KCN in ethanol to make C₆H₅CH₂CN (the chain gains one carbon). Then reduce the nitrile with LiAlH₄ (or H₂/Ni):
C₆H₅CH₂CN + 4[H] → C₆H₅CH₂CH₂NH₂

blocks.prompt:
b) What nitro compound, nitrile and amide are reduced to yield each of the following amine compound?
I) For the primary amine: CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–Nh₂ (determine the structures of nitro compound, nitrile, and amide that would produce this amine upon reduction
ii) For the secondary amine: CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–CH₂–NH–Ch₃
blocks.explanation:
I) Nitro compound (CH₃)₂CHCH₂NO₂; nitrile (CH₃)₂CHCN; amide (CH₃)₂CHCONH₂.
ii) Nitro compounds and nitriles give only primary amines on reduction, so only an amide works here: CH₃CH₂CH₂CONHCH₃ (N-methylbutanamide).
